s1.syndrome_frame: Jaw pain and tooth mobility with radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion
salient_findings: Tender percussion of the right mandibular second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Buccolingual expansion with cortical obliteration on cone beam CT
key_facts: Pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Bony-hard consistency of the buccal and lingual cortices
Lesion extends to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal
Buccolingual expansion with almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex on cone beam CT

shortlist.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and irregular shape

shortlist.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic findings of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with extension to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal

shortlist.label: Radicular cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Tender percussion of both teeth and slight mobility, consistent with a periapical cyst

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion, although less likely given the location and shape

shortlist.label: Simple bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Bony-hard consistency of the buccal and lingual cortices, although less likely given the radiographic findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex, along with its irregular shape, is more characteristic of an odontogenic keratocyst, especially given its potential for aggressive behavior and the patient's age.

rejected.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
rejected.why: While possible, unicystic ameloblastoma tends to be more commonly associated with impacted teeth and may have a more variable radiographic appearance.

rejected.label: Radicular cyst
rejected.why: The lesion's irregular shape and extension beyond the apices of the involved teeth are atypical for a routine periapical cyst or granuloma, making radicular cyst less likely.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: The absence of an associated impacted tooth and the lesion's location and shape make dentigerous cyst an unlikely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Simple bone cyst
rejected.why: Simple bone cysts are typically asymptomatic, found incidentally, and do not usually present with tooth mobility or tenderness, making this diagnosis less likely given the clinical presentation.
